correctness_confidence.basis: Theorem 1 follows from the inspected compiler interface and the checked quadratic transfer; Choi normalization, singular polar factors, the fixed gap and quantifiers are consistent. No material flaw found. Foundational source hardness is cited, not independently re-proved.

rigor.basis: The proof accounts for disjoint gate occurrences, singleton weights, arbitrary starting unitaries, nonattained infima and finite-ancilla convex closures. The distinction between a positive projection matrix and a completely positive subspace map is correct.

novelty.basis: The plausible new combination is a single rational projection cost, a constant undecidability gap and an explicit rational zero-cost bistochastic certificate. Kraus-space distance, factorizable-channel closures, source hardness and most compiler machinery are inherited; targeted primary-source checking does not certify worldwide priority.

significance.basis: A substantive specialist restriction of known noncomputable tracial optimization to an operational channel test. Its substantial dependence on the earlier compiler, variable system dimension and extremely small gap limit claims of broad or practical impact; no field-shaping or historic conclusion is supported.

reproducibility.basis: All 17 manifest entries match and the canonical PDF has eight pages. Both manuscript and both dependency verifiers pass in writable copies, reproducing their JSON files byte-for-byte; 72 additional direct rounding checks pass. There is no end-to-end machine-to-game implementation, global optimization certificate or proof-assistant verification.

summary: The exact eight-page manuscript gives a valid-looking, quantitatively explicit transfer from the supplied relation compiler to projection-cost optimization over channels with unrestricted finite tracial ancillas. I found no unresolved material objection and recommend acceptance as a focused theoretical contribution. The analytic proof, not the finite diagnostics, supports undecidability. The strongest novelty candidate is the simultaneous rational projection, fixed gap and exact bistochastic support certificate; general noncomputability and the distance quantity are established background. This reviewer model family was involved in the manuscript. The operator reports requesting gpt-6-astra with xhigh effort and fork_turns=none; runtime identity and context isolation were not independently attested. No human, certified blind or proof-assistant review is claimed.
strengths: Theorem 1 provides a single real rational projective test with a displayed rational bistochastic zero-cost state supported exactly on its kernel.
Lemma 3 establishes both quadratic transfers with explicit constants and correctly controls repeated labels through disjoint gate occurrences.
The Choi identity includes the correct ancillary m-squared factor, and the soundness proof handles arbitrary projected unitaries and singular polar extensions.
Corollary 4 correctly enumerates all ancilla sizes below a proposed recursive bound; the amplification and semicomputability statements have the right quantifiers.
The manuscript accurately credits prior distance and tracial-optimization results and states its limits on finite attainment, fixed dimension, membership and practical thresholds.
weaknesses: Most of the difficult construction is inherited from the supplied compiler, so the incremental contribution is narrower than the broad undecidability language might initially suggest.
The package reproduces finite identities but does not implement the full machine-to-game map or export a small end-to-end exact channel instance from a source game.
Individual lemma references for the imported compiler interface would improve traceability beyond the present reference to Sections 2–5.
Worldwide priority remains unverified, and the result gives no fixed system dimension or useful practical ancilla/circuit resource estimate.
strong_novelty_candidates: Constant-precision undecidability for a single rational orthogonal projection cost on Choi space, with an explicit rational bistochastic optimizer of the zero-valued semidefinite relaxation and exact support/kernel equality.
The direct quadratic transfer from the balanced relation pencil to the stabilized Yu–Duan–Xu Kraus-space distance, including the uniform reverse rounding of an arbitrary projected unitary.
